The first release of Starwire! If you installed it under its earlier name, Voidlink, this is the same app renamed; it installs separately, so you can uninstall Voidlink afterwards.

Starwire brings the best features of the Android Moonlight clients into one app: Moonlight X's video pipeline, the touchscreen tools from Artemide and Artemis, and favourites from Moonlight V+, Moonlit Artemis and Moonlight X Turnip, with a new space-themed look. It installs next to any Moonlight you already have. The [README](https://github.com/SicarioGaming/Starwire#readme) has the full feature list, a getting-started guide and credits for everything I borrowed.

### What's in it
- **A new look:** the screens take their colour from the game you pick, over a starfield. Apps without cover art, like Desktop and Steam Big Picture, get their own icons.
- **Touchscreen tools:** the floating menu button, the Shortcuts page, pan/zoom, touch modes, the full keyboard, clipboard sharing, PC commands and Virtual Display.
- **Video options:** Warp Drive, Fast V-Sync, LFR and async decoding. I haven't measured how much they change latency in Starwire. There's also an experimental setting to load your own Turnip driver for PyroWave. It's off by default and hasn't been tried with a real Turnip driver yet.
- **Extras:** monitor switching, pinch to zoom anytime, changing the bitrate mid-stream, audio haptics and shortcuts imported from a file.

### Install
Download **Starwire-0.1.0.apk** below on your Android device and open it. Android will ask you to allow installing apps from your browser or file manager. It needs Android 5.0 or newer; PyroWave and the Turnip driver need a 64-bit ARM device. Some features need an Apollo-based host like Vibepollo.

This is the first release, so if something misbehaves, please [open an issue](https://github.com/SicarioGaming/Starwire/issues). I made Starwire with AI: I decided what it should do and how it should look, and Claude Code wrote the code.
